# Self-Service Onboarding Requirements Checklist: Self-Service Farmer Onboarding + First Field

**Purpose**: Review completeness, clarity, consistency, measurable acceptance, and scope of SPEC-001 onboarding requirements and design artifacts.
**Created**: 2026-09-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the rule for deciding whether to present first-field onboarding or skip it for an authenticated farmer with existing fields specified, including the source of that state? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §User Stories 1 and 3; Contract]
- [x] CHK002 Are the hidden default-business behavior and single farmer-visible first-field flow specified without organizational or role setup? [Completeness, Spec §User Stories 1 and 2; FR-001–FR-003]
- [x] CHK003 Does the requirement define one command that ensures the application user, default business, OWNER Membership, and first Field atomically? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002 and FR-015; Plan §Command and transaction design]
- [x] CHK004 Is Membership explicitly the sole ownership authority, with no parallel owner field or client-selected membership? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006 and Permissions; Data Model §Business and Membership]
- [x] CHK005 Are business-scoped creation, authorization, denial, and tenant-isolation expectations stated for the first Field? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006–FR-007 and Observability and Testability]
- [x] CHK006 Does the successful completion response's `FirstFieldSummary` provide post-save confirmation/current first-field state, with general field listing explicitly delegated to SPEC-002? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 2 and FR-024; Contract; Quickstart]
- [x] CHK007 Are logical retry and duplicate-prevention semantics defined independently of the configured Idempotency-Key cache retention? [Completeness, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021 and FR-024; Plan §Transaction and idempotency model]
- [x] CHK008 Are Point/Polygon-only scope, representative-point persistence, optional versioned Polygon boundaries, point-only behavior, and unverified Polygon status consistently specified? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004 and FR-020; Data Model §Field; Contract]
- [x] CHK009 Is the representative-point behavior for polygon-only input defined clearly enough to validate without implying a fabricated boundary? [Clarity, Spec §Validation Rules; Plan §Command and transaction design; Contract]
- [x] CHK010 Is the optional first-field name rule exact for omitted and whitespace-only names after trimming, and are subsequent-field numbering/collision rules assigned to SPEC-002? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019; Data Model §Field; Contract]
- [x] CHK011 Are online-only bootstrap, recoverable connectivity failure, and the point at which success may be shown stated consistently? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015 and FR-018; Contract]
- [x] CHK012 Are all-or-nothing persistence and the no-partial-success outcome on validation or persistence failure specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002 and Validation Rules; Plan §Database transaction boundary]
- [x] CHK013 Does the requirement define the conditions under which form restoration is guaranteed versus best-effort when connectivity is interrupted? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018 and FR-025; Data Model §Temporary onboarding form draft]
- [x] CHK014 Are draft purge events explicitly defined for save, cancellation, sign-out, and account switch, and is draft state distinguished from an offline domain mutation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018 and Mobile and Offline Expectations; Data Model]

## Requirement Clarity and Consistency

- [x] CHK015 Are farmer-facing labels and failure messages required to avoid exposing business bootstrap, Membership, or other internal setup concepts? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009–FR-010 and Failure States]
- [x] CHK016 Are current location, map point, polygon drawing, permission denial, and unavailable-location alternatives described without requiring a single provider? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005 and Failure States; Plan §Required pre-implementation ADRs]
- [x] CHK017 Are mobile progress, weak-connectivity, retry, and saved-state requirements specific enough to prevent false success? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, FR-011, FR-015, and Mobile and Offline Expectations]
- [x] CHK018 Are mobile accessibility expectations specified beyond readable content and touch-usable controls, including any required assistive-technology behavior? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK019 Are privacy-conscious diagnostic events, correlation identifiers, error categories, and prohibited sensitive fields stated consistently? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016 and Observability and Testability]
- [x] CHK020 Are cross-business attempts and permission failures covered by requirements-quality criteria, including denial without revealing another business’s existence? [Coverage, Spec §Permissions and Business Boundary; AGENTS.md §5]

## Acceptance Criteria and Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK021 Are retry and concurrency acceptance criteria clear for lost responses and duplicate submissions, and do they require one logical User/Business/Membership/Field result? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008 and FR-021; SC-003; Quickstart]
- [x] CHK022 Can the primary online flow, alternate location flow, rollback, recovery, and returning-user flow be assessed from the written acceptance scenarios? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories and Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK023 Are SC-001 and SC-002 clearly identified as non-gating pilot targets with usability/pilot evaluation as their measurement method? [Clarity, Spec §Success Criteria; Research §9]
- [x] CHK024 Are SC-003–SC-006 objective enough to assess atomic uniqueness, tenant isolation, mobile completion, and recoverable failure behavior? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK025 Do the OpenAPI contract and quickstart describe the same single completion command, request shape, retry behavior, and committed result as the spec and plan? [Consistency, Contract; Quickstart; Plan]

## Scope, Dependencies, and Assumptions

- [x] CHK026 Is the SPEC-001/SPEC-002 boundary explicit for first-field creation versus later field management, region resolution, and subsequent-field naming policy? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope; Plan §Summary; PRD §60]
- [x] CHK027 Are crop, season, team, weather, satellite, finance, AI, and unrelated module work explicitly excluded from this onboarding slice? [Scope, Spec §Assumptions and Out of Scope; Plan §Summary]
- [x] CHK028 Are ADR-006, ADR-009, and ADR-014 recorded as accepted decisions with Supabase Auth, server-side tenant enforcement, and `react-native-maps` behind their respective adapters? [Dependency, Plan §Approved Architecture Decisions; Research §7]
- [x] CHK029 Is minimum repository scaffolding permitted only where needed for this vertical slice, with unrelated future modules excluded? [Scope, Spec §Out of Scope; Plan §Project Structure; AGENTS.md §26]
- [x] CHK030 Are the PRD’s broader first vertical slice and SPEC-002 field boundary reconciled with the explicitly approved SPEC-001 first-field scope without pulling crop/season work into this feature? [Consistency, Conflict, PRD §55 and §60; Spec §Out of Scope; Plan §Constitution Check]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- This checklist evaluates whether requirements are well specified; it does not verify implementation behavior.
- The planning package contains recommendations and design artifacts plus an executable `tasks.md`; application source implementation remains outstanding.
